# US-01.5 — Import backend modules the same way uvicorn does

|                  |                                                                                |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Epic**         | [EPIC-01 Foundation & Environment](../epics/EPIC-01-foundation-environment.md) |
| **Priority**     | P1                                                                             |
| **Estimate**     | 1                                                                              |
| **Status**       | In progress                                                                    |
| **Owning agent** | `story-builder`                                                                |
| **Files**        | `backend/services/__init__.py`, `backend/tools/__init__.py`                    |

## User story

**As a** developer,
**I want** the backend packages laid out so imports resolve identically in my editor, in tests, and under uvicorn,
**so that** code that runs locally also runs in the container, and nobody loses an hour to an `ImportError`.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — Services package**
Given `backend/` is the working directory,
when I run `python -c "import services.vision_analyzer"`,
then it succeeds.

**AC2 — Tools package**
Given the same,
when I run `python -c "import tools.climate_service"` once [EPIC-03](../epics/EPIC-03-climate-telemetry.md) lands,
then it succeeds — `backend/tools/` exists as a package with an `__init__.py`.

**AC3 — Matches the runtime**
Given uvicorn is started as `uvicorn main:app` from `backend/`,
then the import paths used in source are the ones that resolve at runtime — no `sys.path` manipulation anywhere.

**AC4 — Tests resolve the same modules**
Given `pytest tests` runs from the repository root,
then test modules import the backend packages without each test file patching `sys.path`.

**AC5 — Layering preserved**
Given any module under `services/` or `tools/`,
then it imports neither `main` nor another module from the sibling package.

## Tasks

- [x] `backend/services/__init__.py` exists
- [ ] Create `backend/tools/__init__.py`
- [ ] Decide and document the test import strategy — a `pythonpath` entry in pytest config is preferable to `sys.path` edits in `conftest.py`
- [ ] Confirm `python -c "import services.vision_analyzer"` succeeds from `backend/`

## Current state

`backend/services/` is a proper package. `backend/tools/` **does not exist**, which has two consequences:

| Consequence                                         | Where it bites                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `seed_samples.py` sits at `backend/seed_samples.py` | Inconsistent with the layout in [COPILOT_GUIDE.md](../../../COPILOT_GUIDE.md) |
| `climate_service.py` has nowhere to land            | Blocks [EPIC-03](../epics/EPIC-03-climate-telemetry.md) from starting cleanly |

There is also a live symptom of the import strategy being undecided. `backend/test_analyzer.py` does `from services.vision_analyzer import analyze_urban_hotspot`, which resolves when run from `backend/` but fails when run from the repository root:

```
$ python ./backend/test_analyzer.py     # exit 1
```

That file is retired by [US in EPIC-08](../epics/EPIC-08-quality-assurance.md); the underlying import question belongs here.

## Scope boundary

This story **creates the package**. Physically relocating `seed_samples.py` into it belongs to EPIC-02's seeder story, which is also changing that file's behaviour — doing both in one place would mean two stories editing the same file in the same sprint.

## Test cases

| Test                                      | Asserts                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `test_services_package_importable`        | `import services.vision_analyzer` succeeds                     |
| `test_tools_package_importable`           | `import tools` succeeds                                        |
| `test_no_sys_path_manipulation`           | No `sys.path.append` or `sys.path.insert` in `backend/**/*.py` |
| `test_service_layer_does_not_import_main` | No module in `services/` or `tools/` imports `main`            |

The last two are cheap static assertions and worth keeping — they catch layering violations the moment they appear, which is far cheaper than finding them during EPIC-06's container build.

## Definition of done

Both packages exist, imports resolve identically from `backend/` and from `pytest` at the root, no `sys.path` manipulation exists anywhere, and the four assertions above pass.
